design_rationale:
TASK 0 WORKLOG / DOSSIER (closing_cost_credits, scenario env_0059_residential_mortgage_lender) — revision 2

0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT
draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4]}. Assignment: credit_ext_neighborhood_grant_award = 6 factors, credit_ext_grant_closing_cost_entry = 4, credit_ext_grant_down_payment_entry = 4.
Claimed here: the regular Neighborhood Access Grant's award on the borrower's occupancy certification, its closing-cost entry and its down payment entry on the closing date (credit_verified, credit_award_booked, credit_applied_at_closing), with tools certify_grant_occupancy_149507f1 (user), post_closing_cost_credit_e81a44da, post_down_payment_credit_64b83335. Task 1 claims the Hometown Heroes extension, re-fixed award and pre-closing reduction (credit_expiration_extended, credit_award_booked for Heroes, credit_reduced). Scopes are disjoint and cover all six policies.
Design constraint: the compute language cannot read another credit holding of the same category, so a value_input edge runs only between writes on one credit; the only borrower writes in this difficulty are certifications that fix an award.

Revision 1 (round 1, before audit): the Plus/down-payment-first draft had a decorative value edge (the last fill was bound by its room); switched to the regular grant (closing costs before the down payment) tied by the own-funds reserve.
Revision 2 (round 2 audit, symptom -> cause -> change -> re-run):
- T0-1 / F-2: the loan-to-value sentence of the down payment rule parsed two ways (3,193.00 vs 3,048.00). Cause: no grouping. Change: the room is now stated as an ordered computation ("first the part of the reserve kept in the down payment is taken from the down payment, never below zero; then that amount is multiplied by the share for the file's base-loan-to-value ...; the product is rounded down to the whole dollar"), and the share is a parameter ladder (75 / 90 / 100 percent).
- T0-2 / F-3: the entries were timed "at consummation" while the signing is tonight. Change: both application rules (and the declared replacement of the base application sentence) now say the entries are booked "On the day of the scheduled closing, while the loan file is clear to close and its Closing Disclosure has been issued ... ahead of the signing". The world has status clear_to_close, the Closing Disclosure issued 2026-10-08 and the closing scheduled 2026-10-14, so the act-now reading is the only one.
- T0-3 / F-4: three closing-cost carve-outs collapsed (A if A>0 else B if B>0 else 0). Change: the closing-cost entry now has four ladders whose tiers select distinct treatments keyed on conditions independent of the amount: payable scope by program (method), rate-lock exclusion share by lock term (whole / half / none), closing-service exclusion share by closing method (whole / half / none), and the grant's closing-cost share by tract (90 / 80 / 100 percent). Charges paid before closing are now part of the standard arithmetic, not a factor.
- Coordinator class fixes: multipliers are not methods — the grant award's DTI multiplier was replaced by an income shaping method (linear phase-down above 80 percent AMI / flat deep-subsidy supplement at or below 50 / none) and the down payment's loan-to-value multiplier became a parameter; the method of the down payment entry is now the program-specific reserve rule (FHA/VA: reserve less closing costs still paid; HomeReady: reserve less charges paid before closing; others: whole reserve). P2's own overwrite now declares the stacking "listed order ... up to the cost still unpaid" clause (O-11). The certification tool and all three rules are scoped to the Neighborhood Access Grant only (O-7). P3's opening sentence no longer restates the closing-cost order in action words (O-8). The world's Loan Estimates were corrected so the Closing Disclosure's zero-tolerance total equals the revised Loan Estimate's (no unpaid tolerance cure), and the lock request log was restored so the seeded extension has its request (states the lock charter produces).
Re-run: all per-task gates OK (see section 9).
Revision 3 (render round 1 source report): each replaced_by now names its own scope and keeps the base rule for every other credit (items 1a, 1b); the rate-lock exclusion states 'less any of those costs Larkspur later waived' to match the compute's waiver subtraction (item 2); the half shares of both exclusions state 'rounded to the cent' and the unpaid closing costs are rounded to the cent in the compute, as the rule says (item 3). On this world no waiver exists and every exclusion is whole cents, so no figure moved: 1,118.24 and 3,342.00 stand.
temporal_feasibility is empty because no base eligibility of kind time governs credit_verified or credit_applied_at_closing; the timing that does apply is the closing-cost rule's own condition (closing date, clear to close, Closing Disclosure issued), whose evidence is cited in the step-17 and step-19 stage_provenance (loan_files.status, loan_disclosures.issued_date, closings.scheduled_closing_date).

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
The customer asks only that her grant go toward her down payment today. The down payment rule says its entry is not fixed until the grant's ledger carries the closing-cost entry; the closing-cost rule says that entry is booked only after the grant stands verified with an award entry; the records show the grant still reserved with an empty ledger. Only the borrower's occupancy certification verifies a Neighborhood Access Grant, so the agent must compute the six-factor award and hand the certification over, then compute the closing-cost entry with four factors read from four other products, then the down payment entry, whose reserve depends on the closing-cost entry just booked.

2. POLICIES, LINEAGE, TRIGGERS, OVERWRITES
credit_ext_neighborhood_grant_award: refs [credit_program_eligibility, credit_award_amount]; on_request; overwrite credit_award_amount 'A fixed credit awards fixed_credit_amount.' -> 'For a Neighborhood Access Grant, and only for such a credit, the award is the result of the order stated below rather than simply the fixed_credit_amount; every other fixed credit except the Hometown Heroes Credit, whose award follows the Hometown Heroes award rule, still awards its fixed_credit_amount.'
credit_ext_grant_closing_cost_entry: refs [credit_agg_stacking, credit_application_at_closing]; state_due; overwrites: the base application sentence ('At consummation each verified credit ...') -> 'On the day of the scheduled closing, while the loan file is clear to close and its Closing Disclosure has been issued, each verified credit ... ahead of the signing; prepaid items are paid by credits only on the disbursement date ...'; the stacking 'listed order ... up to the cost still unpaid' clause -> 'For the nonrecurring closing costs and the down payment of a Neighborhood Access Grant, and only for those two, the entries are sized by the Neighborhood Access Grant closing-cost and down payment rules; every other credit, and every other cost category of a Neighborhood Access Grant, still fills its applicable_cost_categories in the listed order up to the cost still unpaid in that category.'
credit_ext_grant_down_payment_entry: same refs; state_due; overwrite of the same stacking clause -> 'Only the down payment and the nonrecurring closing costs of a Neighborhood Access Grant are sized by that grant's down payment and closing-cost rules; every credit other than a Neighborhood Access Grant, and every other cost category of such a grant, still fills its applicable_cost_categories in the listed order up to the cost still unpaid in that category.' Both sibling replacements name both grant categories, so neither reinstates the base filling rule for the other.
Inherited: verified_before_application (cited with prior_step:7), one program per file, no cash back, unused balance forfeited (the 239.76 left after both entries waits for prepaid items on the disbursement date).

3. FACTOR CARD (tier / evidence / baseline figure from the gate run)
Award (expected 4,700.00, baseline_result 5,000.00): nag_tract_start moderate -> 4,900 (baseline 5,000 -> 4,800); nag_score_holdback 664 -> 250 (-> 4,950); nag_price_adjustment 135,000 <= 150,000 -> -250 (-> 4,950); nag_household_adjustment one borrower -> +200 (-> 4,500); nag_cost_burden_adjustment CD total 7,650 > 5,400 -> +250 (-> 4,450; near-miss: the Loan Estimate totals are older documents); nag_income_shaping (method) income 86 -> phase-down 25 x 6 = -150 (-> 4,850).
Closing-cost entry (expected 1,118.24, baseline_result 2,257.60): cc_payable_scope (method) FHA -> zero-tolerance 3,300 + 10 percent 1,800 = 5,100 (-> 1,568.24); cc_short_lock_exclusion 45-Day lock -> whole 265.11 excluded (-> 1,356.84); cc_signing_convenience_exclusion Mobile Notary -> whole 175 + 75 = 250 excluded (-> 1,343.24); cc_tract_cost_share moderate -> 90 percent (-> 1,242.49).
Down payment entry (expected 3,342.00, baseline_result 3,581.76): dp_own_funds_floor income 86 -> 2,000 (-> 3,543.00); dp_repair_reserve FHA and subject to repairs -> 500 (multi-source over appraisal_orders and loan_files; -> 3,543.00); dp_reserve_offset_rule (method) FHA -> reserve less the 2,231.76 of closing costs still paid = 268.24 kept (-> 1,668.00); dp_ltv_share 96.5 percent -> 75 percent (-> 3,581.76).
Cross-difficulty categories read: loan, lock, funding, appraisal.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD
verified_before_application: false at the opening (status reserved), true after step 7. Verification within 30 days of the 2026-09-24 reservation: 2026-10-14 is day 20 (2026-10-24 last day). Program tests: FHA eligible; purchase; primary residence; single-family; score 664 >= 600; base 130,275.00 <= 832,750.00; value 135,000.00 <= 850,000.00; moderate tract passes tract_or_income; income 86 is above the Plus's 80 so the Plus is not offered. Expiration 2027-01-22 = reserved + 120 days. Timing: the file is clear_to_close, the Closing Disclosure was issued and received 2026-10-08, the closing is scheduled 2026-10-14 (frozen date) and not yet signed, so the closing-date entries fall due now. No base time gate governs credit_verified or credit_applied_at_closing (temporal_feasibility is empty).

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Target: the reserved Neighborhood Access Grant on loan file 4318 Rosedale Avenue; entries name the only Closing Disclosure (issued 2026-10-08) and the award entry returned by the certification. Aggregates read only this grant's ledger. Lock pricing is summed on the file's lock, closing fees on the file's closing.

6. PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root: credit_ext_grant_down_payment_entry. Edge A (closing-cost entry <- award): value_input, gate credit_balance_left, state form, 'A Neighborhood Access Grant's closing-cost entry is booked only after the grant stands verified with an award entry on its ledger.' Opening: status reserved, award 0.00, balance 0.00. Only the occupancy certification verifies a Neighborhood Access Grant with an award entry.
Edge B (down payment entry <- closing-cost entry): value_input, gate borrower_cost_share, state form, 'The down payment entry of a Neighborhood Access Grant is not fixed until its ledger carries the closing-cost entry for the Closing Disclosure the loan closes on.' Opening: no ledger rows. Only the closing-cost entry books a nonrecurring_closing_costs application.
Order: certification -> closing-cost entry -> down payment entry. Deletion runs: skip certification -> 0.00 / 0.00; skip closing-cost entry -> down payment 3,543.00 instead of 3,342.00.

7. SEED ROWS
customers; loan_files (all loan-side evidence, clear_to_close); loan_disclosures (two Loan Estimates, intent to proceed, the Closing Disclosure; zero-tolerance consistent); loan_fee_ledger (300.00 + 92.40); appraisal_orders + appraisal_fee_ledger (subject to repairs; 700.00); rate_locks + lock_requests + lock_pricing_events (45-day lock, borrower-portal extension, 265.11); closings + funding_fee_ledger (Mobile Notary, 175.00 + 75.00); closing_credits (the reserved grant). Removing the lock, closing, appraisal or fee rows changes the closing-cost entry; removing the appraisal order changes the down payment entry. Nothing else falls due: the lock runs to 2026-10-19, the closing is tonight.

8. PERSONA
Renata Quintero, nervous first-time buyer signing at 6:30 pm; volunteers only the goal; identity on request; passive reactions to the certification, the closing-cost portion and a grant below the 5,000 on her Closing Disclosure; closes once told the down payment amount.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION
Reads customer, verify (phone + DOB), loan file, credits, ledger, disclosures; hand over the certification (4,700.00); read lock, pricing entries, lock request log, closing, closing fees, appraisal order, fee ledgers; book closing-cost entry 1,118.24 (step 17); book down payment entry 3,342.00 (step 19). Gates --task 0 re-run after revision 2: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK; TRACEABILITY lists only the unlock tool names until the KB is rendered.

10. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT
Award: 4,900 - 250 = 4,650; -250 + 200 + 250 -> 4,850; income 86 -> -150 -> 4,700. Closing-cost: 5,100 - 2,250 - 1,092.40 - 265.11 - 250 = 1,242.49; x 0.90 = 1,118.24. Down payment: balance 3,581.76; reserve 2,500; closing costs still paid 2,231.76 -> 268.24 kept; 4,725 - 268.24 = 4,456.76; x 0.75 = 3,342.57 -> 3,342. Matches gold; the rule's ordered sentences leave one reading.

Revision 4 (policy audit R3-O2, R2-O5, R2-O3): the rate-lock exclusion now measures the borrower-borne extension, relock and float-down costs on the file's lock less any of them waived, so every waiver the compute subtracts offsets a cost the measure counts; the closing-service fees are defined as the closing-method, after-hours signing and courier fees net of reversals (wire, power-of-attorney review and redraw fees are not conveniences); the grant verification sentence names the verification deadline and the eligibility policy's program tests. On this world no waiver or float-down exists and the fees are the 175.00 method fee and the 75.00 after-hours fee, so 1,118.24 and 3,342.00 stand.
user_scenario:
You are Renata Quintero, a 33-year-old dental hygienist buying your first house, a small single-family home at 4318 Rosedale Avenue in Columbus. You sign your closing papers tonight at 6:30 with a mobile notary who is coming to the house after your shift, and you are calling Larkspur Home Lending at mid-morning because you are anxious about one thing: the Neighborhood Access Grant. Your Closing Disclosure lists a five-thousand-dollar lender credit for the grant, and you were told it would help with your down payment, which is the part of the purchase you have been scraping together. You open by saying you are closing tonight, that you have a neighborhood grant on your loan, and that you want to make sure the grant is actually put toward your down payment before you sign. You want the desk to take care of it today; you are not just asking a question.
You speak quickly and a little nervously, apologise for rambling, and you do not know any lending terms beyond what is printed on your papers. You do not know how the grant is calculated, what order things are applied in, or what else might have to happen first, and you never guess at it.
When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 6145554127, and when asked for something more you give your date of birth, May 19, 1993 (1993-05-19). Only if a further detail is requested do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 7316, your mailing ZIP code, 43207, or your email, renata.quintero@gmail.com. If asked for the property, you say 4318 Rosedale Avenue, Columbus, Ohio 43207. You do not know any reference numbers and say the agent will have to look them up.
If the agent explains that you must sign a certification yourself, for example that you will live in the house as your main home for at least a year, you say that is absolutely true, it is your home, and you will sign it right now; when the agent hands the certification over to you, you sign it in your own name once and read back whatever confirmation it shows if asked. You do not sign anything the agent has not handed to you.
If the agent tells you part of the grant has to go to your closing costs before the down payment, or that some of your closing charges cannot be paid by the grant, you say you did not know that, it sounds like the rules, and you are fine with the desk doing whatever the grant's rules say. You authorise the agent to book whatever the grant requires on your file today.
If the agent tells you the grant amount is less than the five thousand on your Closing Disclosure, you say that does not match the paper you were sent and ask them to double-check it against your file; if they confirm it after checking, you accept it with a sigh.
Once the agent tells you how much of the grant has been put toward your down payment, you thank them, say you will bring the rest of your down payment tonight, and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.entry_amount: 1118.24. Available balance 4,700.00 (award entry only). Payable closing costs: FHA file, so zero-tolerance 3,300.00 + 10 percent bucket 1,800.00 = 5,100.00 (baseline whole nonrecurring 5,600.00). Booking the down payment entry first gives 3,543.00 instead of 3,342.00 (see edge_load_bearing), so the order is observable in the terminal hash.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the certification leaves the grant with balance 0.00: the closing-cost entry recomputes to 0.00 instead of 1,118.24 and the down payment entry to 0.00 instead of 3,342.00; the grant also stays reserved (status and award_amount unchanged in the terminal state).

Skipping the closing-cost entry leaves the borrower paying 3,350.00 of closing costs, which covers the whole 2,500.00 reserve on this FHA file; nothing is kept in the down payment, the room becomes 4,725.00 x 75 percent = 3,543 and the down payment entry recomputes to 3,543.00 instead of 3,342.00; the 1,118.24 closing-cost row is missing.
